name: Congenital Muscular Dystrophy due to Dystroglycanopathy
aliases: CMD with Defective Glycosylation of α-Dystroglycan

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Muscular Dystrophy due to Dystroglycanopathy

criteria.description: Early-onset hypotonia and muscle weakness presenting in infancy
Muscle biopsy showing reduced or absent glycosylation of α-dystroglycan
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in α-dystroglycan glycosylation (e.g., POMT1, POMT2, FKRP)
MRI demonstrating structural brain abnormalities such as cobblestone lissencephaly or cerebellar hypoplasia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early-onset hypotonia and muscle weakness plus either muscle biopsy evidence of α-dystroglycan hypoglycosylation or pathogenic variants in dystroglycanopathy-related genes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Brain MRI findings support diagnosis but are not mandatory.

searchTerms: low muscle tone and weakness from birth
muscle weakness and hypotonia present at birth
abnormal sugar modification of muscle protein
improper sugar attachment on muscle protein

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cerebellar hypoplasia or cobblestone lissencephaly on brain MRI
searchTerms: small cerebellum or cobblestone brain on MRI
brain imaging shows cerebellar hypoplasia or cobblestone pattern
abnormal brain structure with cerebellar underdevelopment
cognitive impairment ranging mild to severe

common.symptomName: Ocular abnormalities including myopia and strabismus
searchTerms: eye problems including nearsightedness and crossed eyes

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness
searchTerms: respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness
difficulty breathing caused by muscle weakness
skin problems like dry, scaly skin

laboratory: Reduced or absent glycosylation of α-dystroglycan on muscle biopsy immunohistochemistry
imaging: Brain MRI showing cobblestone lissencephaly, cerebellar hypoplasia, or other structural abnormalities
Muscle MRI demonstrating muscle atrophy and fatty infiltration
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes involved in α-dystroglycan glycosylation (e.g., POMT1, POMT2, FKRP, FKTN, ISPD)

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of merosin (laminin α2) on muscle biopsy
Lack of brain malformations typical of dystroglycanopathies
Severe brain malformations including hydrocephalus and encephalocele
More profound developmental delay and early lethality

redFlags: Severe hypotonia with respiratory failure in neonatal period
Progressive muscle weakness with joint contractures
Structural brain abnormalities on MRI suggestive of cobblestone lissencephaly
references: Mercuri E, Muntoni F. Muscular Dystrophies. Lancet. 2013;381(9869):845-860.
Godfrey C, Foley AR, Clement E, Muntoni F. Dystroglycanopathies: coming into focus. Curr Opin Genet Dev. 2011;21(3):278-285.
